subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematical Methods, Units 1 and 2
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Mathematical Methods Units 1 and 2

units.title: Unit 1: Polynomial and power functions, rates of change and counting

points.title: Relations and functions
points.brief: A function gives one output for each input. Function notation f(x) names the rule, with a domain and range.

points.title: Domain and range notation
points.brief: Intervals use brackets, such as [0, 5) including 0 but not 5, and a restricted domain can be written f: [0, ∞) → R.

points.title: Inverse functions
points.brief: An inverse reverses a function by swapping x and y. It exists only when the function is one-to-one, and its graph reflects in y = x.

points.title: Reading graphs of real data
points.brief: Describing where a graph of real data rises, falls, levels off or crosses an axis, even without a rule for it.

points.title: Linear graphs and equations
points.brief: Lines y = mx + c, gradients, parallel lines (equal gradients) and perpendicular lines (gradients multiplying to −1).

points.title: Quadratic graphs
points.brief: Turning point form y = a(x − h)² + k shows the vertex (h, k). Intercepts come from factorising or the quadratic formula.

points.title: The discriminant
points.brief: b² − 4ac decides whether a quadratic has two, one or no real roots.

points.title: Cubic and quartic graphs
points.brief: Factorised polynomials show their x-intercepts. Repeated factors touch or flatten at the axis.

points.title: Power functions
points.brief: Graphs such as y = 1/x, y = 1/x² and y = √x have asymptotes or start points that set their shape.

points.title: Expanding and factorising
points.brief: Common factors, grouping, difference of two squares and perfect squares rewrite polynomials.

points.title: Dividing polynomials
points.brief: Long division writes P(x) as a divisor times a quotient plus a remainder.

points.title: The remainder and factor theorems
points.brief: Substituting a value into a polynomial gives the remainder on dividing by (x - a). A remainder of 0 means a factor, and the rational root theorem lists possible roots.

points.title: Solving polynomial equations
points.brief: Factorise, then set each factor to zero. The factor theorem finds a first factor for a cubic.

points.title: The bisection method
points.brief: Halving an interval again and again where a function changes sign closes in on a root to any accuracy.

points.title: Transformations of graphs
points.brief: Dilations from or parallel to an axis, reflections in an axis and translations move and reshape a graph in predictable ways.

points.title: Families of functions
points.brief: A parameter in a rule, such as a in y = ax^2, describes a whole family of graphs, and given points find a particular rule.

points.title: Simultaneous equations
points.brief: Solve two equations together by substitution or elimination, including a line meeting a parabola.

points.title: Average rate of change
points.brief: The gradient of the chord between two points, (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).

points.title: Instantaneous rate of change
points.brief: The gradient of the tangent at a point, found as the limit of chord gradients as the points move together.

points.title: Rates in context
points.brief: Reading rates from graphs of real data, such as temperature over time, motion graphs or water filling containers of different shapes.

points.title: Tangent lines
points.brief: The gradient of the tangent at a point measures the instantaneous rate of change, and shows where it is positive, negative or zero.

points.title: Sample spaces and events
points.brief: The sample space lists every outcome. An event is a set of outcomes, with probability from 0 to 1.

points.title: Simulation
points.brief: Coins, dice, spinners and random number generators simulate experiments, and the results estimate probabilities.

points.title: Counting principles
points.brief: The addition principle counts choices that are alternatives; the multiplication principle counts choices made one after another.

points.title: Combinations
points.brief: The number of selections of r items from n, when order does not matter, is nCr = n!/(r!(n − r)!).

units.title: Unit 2: Circular, exponential and logarithmic functions, calculus and probability

points.title: Radians
points.brief: An angle measured by arc length on a unit circle. A full turn is 2π radians, and arc length is radius times angle.

points.title: The unit circle
points.brief: A point on the unit circle at angle θ has coordinates (cos θ, sin θ), which gives the signs in each quadrant.

points.title: Exact values
points.brief: The sine, cosine and tangent of π/6, π/4 and π/3 have exact values from two special triangles.

points.title: Symmetry and periodicity
points.brief: Sine, cosine and tangent repeat and reflect around the unit circle, which links values in different quadrants.

points.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
points.brief: Graphs of y = a sin(nx) + k and y = a cos(nx) + k, where a sets the amplitude, n the period and k the mean value.

points.title: The tangent graph
points.brief: y = tan x has period π and vertical asymptotes where cos x = 0.

points.title: Modelling with sine and cosine
points.brief: Tides, daylight hours and temperatures can be modelled with sine and cosine, where period, amplitude and mean have meaning.

points.title: Solving trigonometric equations
points.brief: Find a reference angle, then every solution in the domain using the quadrants and the period.

points.title: Index laws
points.brief: Rules such as a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) and (a^m)^n = a^(mn) simplify expressions with powers.

points.title: Exponential graphs
points.brief: y = a^x has a horizontal asymptote at y = 0 and passes through (0, 1). It grows for a > 1 and decays for 0 < a < 1.

points.title: Logarithms
points.brief: A logarithm is an exponent: log base a of x is the power of a that gives x. The log function is the inverse of the exponential.

points.title: Logarithm laws
points.brief: log(ab) = log a + log b, log(a/b) = log a − log b, and log(a^n) = n log a.

points.title: Solving exponential equations
points.brief: Equations such as 2^x = 10 are solved by taking logarithms of both sides.

points.title: Exponential models
points.brief: Exponential rules model growth and decay, with an initial value, a growth or decay rate, a doubling time or a half-life.

points.title: Differentiation from first principles
points.brief: The derivative is the limit of the gradient of a chord as its two points come together.

points.title: The central difference approximation
points.brief: The gradient of a chord either side of a point, f(x + h) - f(x - h) over 2h, estimates the derivative.

points.title: Differentiating polynomials
points.brief: The derivative of x^n is n x^(n−1), and derivatives of sums are sums of derivatives.

points.title: Graphs of derivative functions
points.brief: f′ is positive where f rises, negative where it falls and zero at stationary points.

points.title: Stationary points
points.brief: Where the derivative is zero, a graph has a local maximum, local minimum or stationary point of inflection. These solve maximum and minimum problems.

points.title: Antidifferentiation
points.brief: Reversing differentiation gives a family of curves with the same gradient. A known point picks out one of them.

points.title: Newton's method
points.brief: Following tangent lines towards the axis improves a guess at a root of a cubic again and again.

points.title: Venn diagrams and Karnaugh maps
points.brief: Venn diagrams and probability tables organise events and show unions, intersections and complements.

points.title: The addition rule
points.brief: Pr(A ∪ B) = Pr(A) + Pr(B) − Pr(A ∩ B). For mutually exclusive events the last term is zero.

points.title: Conditional probability
points.brief: Pr(A | B) = Pr(A ∩ B)/Pr(B), the chance of A given that B has happened.

points.title: The law of total probability
points.brief: The probability of an event is the sum of its probabilities along each path, such as given A and given not A.

points.title: Independent events
points.brief: A and B are independent when Pr(A ∩ B) = Pr(A) × Pr(B).

points.title: Tree diagrams
points.brief: Branches show each stage of an experiment. Multiplying along branches gives probabilities, with or without replacement.
